title: Graduated margin-aware canary harbor with drift attenuation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a canary orchestration pattern (the 'Canary Harbor') that graduations exposure based on margin-aware metrics and continuous drift attenuation. This ticket scopes the product spec for experiment setup, exposure control, per-request quality gating, statistical early-stop checks, shadow piping, and an auto-revert control loop. The goal is to give product and platform teams a single, auditable flow for progressive model upgrades that reacts to signal quality and distributional drift rather than just aggregate deltas.
business_justification: Current rollouts are either too manual or use simple aggregate gates that miss per-cohort regressions and early drift. This feature reduces outage risk, shortens safe time-to-50% exposure for high-confidence upgrades, and lowers ops overhead for rollback decisions. Expected ROI: fewer manual rollbacks, faster adoption of improved models, and reduced user-facing regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) UI/DSL to create a Canary Harbor experiment with knobs for start_exposure, max_exposure, margin_thresholds, and drift_decay_rate. 2) Exposure thermostat that increases exposure in graduated steps when margin signals are within thresholds and pauses/inverts on sustained drift. 3) Per-request quality gating that tags and isolates low-confidence outputs into shadow capture. 4) Statistical engine implements sequential testing (alpha spending) + cohort-aware checks and will trigger a safe auto-revert policy when pre-defined triggers fire. 5) End-to-end integration tests, one integration run on staging with real traffic replay, and documentation and example templates in the Console. 6) Audit logs and a dashboard tile showing exposure timeline, margin signals, and triggered actions.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Product API design and backend schema (2 sprints). Phase 2: Implement exposure thermostat service and sequential stats library (3 sprints). Phase 3: Per-request gating + shadow capture plumbing and storage; wire to observability. Phase 4: Console surfaces, rollout templates, and integration tests. Phase 5: Staged rollout to beta customers and instrumentation adjustments. Key deliverables: API spec, metrics spec, rollout policy DSL, canary orchestration service, console UI, and runbook.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dogfood: run experimental Harbor on non-critical feature with small cohort (1% traffic) for 2 weeks. 2) Beta customers opt-in: expose to 5 customers with manual supervision. 3) Gradual activation: enable auto-revert in 'monitor-only' mode first (no enforced rollback). 4) Full auto-revert: turn on enforcement after 4 weeks and confidence checks pass. Each step includes post-mortem and signal tuning.
metrics_and_checks: - Primary metrics: user-facing error rate, semantic-similarity regression (paired baseline vs candidate), latency P99 delta. - Margin signals: moving average of per-request quality score and margin to baseline. - Statistical checks: sequential testing with O'Brien-Fleming alpha spending, cohort-stratified p-values, and FDR control across multiple metrics. - Drift attenuation: KL-divergence on request features with exponential decay; if KL > drift_threshold for drift_decay_window, freeze exposure. - Auto-revert triggers: sustained metric breach for 3 consecutive evaluation windows OR single catastrophic event breach (customer-impact high). - Instrumentation: sample sizes per window, power estimates, and warning thresholds in Console.
testing_plan: Unit tests for thermostat decision logic and sequential-test math
Integration test with synthetic traffic replay (edge cases: low-sample cohorts, noisy signals)
Canary run in staging with golden baseline for 72 hours
Chaos test: simulate partial service degradation and verify safe fallback to baseline
End-to-end runbook walkthrough with SRE and Solutions for rollback confirmation
observability_and_alerting: Expose time-series for exposure fraction, margin signal, per-cohort p-values, and drift scores. Alerts: (1) margin-warning (soft) at step threshold, (2) freeze-and-investigate at sustained drift threshold, (3) auto-revert executed — actionable runbook link. Dashboard tile to visualize stepwise exposure and recent decision events.
open_questions: Q1: Which quality signal should be the canonical 'margin' for early MVP? (semantic-similarity vs. task-specific correctness)
Q2: Default alpha spending schedule — start with conservative OBF or use Pocock-style?
Q3: How to surface per-customer opt-outs for auto-revert enforcement?
Q4: Storage retention for shadow-captured low-confidence requests (privacy/compliance limits)?
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives from low-sample cohorts triggering premature revert. Mitigation: require minimum sample thresholds and cohort-aware smoothing. Risk: noisy per-request quality signals exploited by adversarial inputs. Mitigation: combine signal with input-distribution drift checks and manual review for high-impact rollbacks.
out_of_scope: Full experiment cataloging for all historical rollouts (we'll surface current and last-30d only), and automated remediation that rewrites prompts or model weights (future work).
follow_up_tasks: Create a JIRA epic for ENG workstreams (ENG-xxxxx)
Schedule an SRE tabletop for the auto-revert runbook
Prototype margin scoring library and publish API contract
Draft Console UX mockups and add to design review cycle
notes: This approach intentionally blends conservative statistical rigor (sequential tests, cohort stratification) with operational heuristics (thermostat-style exposure and drift decay). The 'harbor' metaphor emphasizes a safe staging area where candidate models can anchor while traffic is gradually admitted. Keep API flexible to add new margin signals later.
